newsitem.title: USA: Roberts, Landrieu, Johnson new on Senate ag panel.
newsitem.headline: Roberts, Landrieu, Johnson new on Senate ag panel.

text.p: The only newcomers on the U.S. Senate Agriculture Committee will be Republican Pat Roberts and Democrats Mary Landrieu and Tim Johnson, a committee staff worker said Monday.
Appointments to the panel will not become official until the Senate reconvenes in January but, the staffer said, "it should be pretty routine now."
The panel would have 10 Republicans and eight Democrats.
Roberts, Landrieu and Johnson were elected in November. As House Agriculture chairman, Roberts of Kansas was author of the "Freedom to Farm" plan.
Indiana Republican Richard Lugar would be chairman for a second term. Iowan Tom Harkin will be the Democratic leader.

Republicans on the panel were expected to be Lugar, Jesse Helms of North Carolina, Thad Cochran of Mississippi, Mitch McConnell of Kentucky, Larry Craig of Idaho, Paul Coverdell of Georgia, Rick Santorum of Pennsylvania, Charles Grassley of Iowa, Phil Gramm of Texas and Roberts.

Democrats would be Harkin, Pat Leahy of Vermont, Kent Conrad of North Dakota, Tom Daschle of South Dakota, Max Baucus of Montana, Bob Kerrey of Nebraska, Landrieu of Louisiana and Johnson of South Dakota.

The appointment of Daschle and Johnson to the committee would be something of a rarity because it is not common for both senators from a state to be on the same committee, let alone both from the same party.
